models.title: Historical Cockcroft–Gault creatinine-clearance arithmetic with explicit dimensional divisor
models.summary: Correction superseding b02/r1 and b05/r2. Addresses reviewerAA by an explicit calibrated-domain limitation and NKF historical context, and mechanical staging failure by replacing the dimensional bare divisor with supplied empirical input K in seconds. No new serum-creatinine bounds or clinical validation are claimed.

relationship.original_equation: eClcr = ((140-age)*weight)/(72*SCr), multiplied by0.85 if female; eClcr[mL/min], age[years], weight[kg], SCr[mg/dL].
relationship.locator: Q16, printed8 / PDF index7; historical context begins printed7 / PDF index6.
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced a,w,sCr,C map to age,weight,SCr,eClcr; z encodes the stated branch, so1-0.15*z reproduces1 or0.85. Introduced K carries the source empirical72-form coefficient normalized into seconds: sCr[mg/dL]=100*sCr[kg/m^3] and1 mL/min=1e-6/60 m^3/s, hence K=72*100*60*1e6 s=432000000000 s. These are a derivation of a dimensional parameter value, not conversion factors in the executable expression. Dimensional check: (dimensionless)*M/(T*(M/L^3))=L^3/T; mass scale cancels under both coherent SI and the kit kWh-based mass convention. Pure1 is branch identity;140 is the source age-index intercept;0.15 is1-0.85. K is never solved for or inferred from the patient. Guards on K use positivity only, avoiding dimensionally invalid equality to a bare seconds literal.

assumptions: Source scope: White-men derivation, ages18–92; NKF attests measured creatinine-clearance coverage approximately30–130 mL/min and pre-standardization serum assays (FAQ Q16/Table3; original abstract).

Calibrated-domain limitation: guards express algebraic admissibility only. Scientific interpretation requires independent confirmation of matching historical population, stable assessment and assay calibration; a positive sCr alone is insufficient.

Parameter profile: caller supplies the evidenced historical K=432000000000 s; K is an explicit empirical parameter because literals carry no dimensions. It is not a freely selectable duration or an authorized recalibration.

Application profile: this is forward arithmetic for qualified interpretation; it does not select treatment, drug dose or monitoring. Female-branch calculations are formal arithmetic only, without a validated female-population claim.
limitations: No inspected source establishes serum-creatinine calibration endpoints. The approximately30–130 mL/min range concerns measured clearance, not sCr or a guard on the predicted output; no concentration interval is invented or inferred from it.

The historical equation is not expressed for standardized creatinine. Modern IDMS-traceable measurements are not assumed interchangeable; no assay conversion is supplied. Broader-population and female validation are not established.
Measured creatinine clearance and measured GFR differ. This output is not BSA-indexed, is not a GFR measurement, and must not be bound to GFR solely because units match.

Original abstract reports correlation0.83 against mean paired24-hour clearances in236 patients; no individual error bound or confidence interval is asserted. Numerical checks validate transcription/unit handling, not clinical accuracy.

K positivity does not enforce version matching; caller/reviewer must verify the coefficient provenance and all non-scalar applicability conditions. Inverse solving for K or patient inputs is excluded from this return.

references.method: Independent conventional-unit route:1.2 mg/dL; (140-50)*72/(72*1.2)=75 mL/min; converting the exact rational75/60000000 gives1.25e-6 m^3/s. Absolute1e-18 m^3/s covers binary floating arithmetic, not empirical uncertainty.
